data.name: Introvert Quest
data.detailed_description:
Introvert Quest is a comedy based JRPG set in a fictional, modern setting. In it, the player will experience the life of a socially awkward shut-in named Bryce Han, who is pushed into (for him Herculean) tasks by his therapist and friend of his late father, Dr. Abe Eisner.

Through the intensive four day therapy, the player will tackle tasks such as: going to the store, making new friends, finding a part time job and many more. But, even such menial tasks can hold may dangers of a big city for one not used to its streets. Scammers, beggars and delinquents lurk around every corner waiting for unsuspecting targets.

Make friends and enemies in this twisted modern day RPG where every day activities seem like a grueling tasks for the player to deal with. Be careful what you do or say for every choice will have some consequences in the future, for the past choices cannot be rewritten!

The gameplay of Introvert Quest will feature mostly dialogue based adventuring, concentrated on a multiple choice system. Choices will impact future events and interaction with other characters inhabiting Sky City. Introvert Quest also features JRPG style battles, but not as a main focus (mostly optional, plus an entire optional mini game aspect: Digital Duels a game that a lot of people play). Battles will be turn based with highly animated attacks. And lastly, but most importantly, after finishing the game successfully, the player will be thrust into a new, completely different experience.

FEATURES

 Branching storyline
 Multiple choices that impact the story
 Action packed turn based battles
 Big city to explore which unlocks as the hero gains more and more confidence
 Hyperbole version of various human weaknesses
 Form social links with other inhabitants of he city
 Love life and your fellow man!
 New Game + with a lot of new content

reviews.review:
Introvert Quest is the kind of independent RPG that immediately distinguishes itself through its premise alone. Developed and published by Amaterasu Software, the game abandons fantasy kingdoms and world-ending threats in favor of something far more grounded: the everyday struggles of an introverted young man trying to function in society. Set in the bustling Sky City, the story follows Bryce Han, a recluse who has spent much of his life avoiding social interaction. Concerned about his isolated lifestyle, his family arranges for him to undergo a four-day therapy program designed to push him beyond the safety of his home. What follows is an adventure that turns routine tasks into significant milestones, creating an experience that is equal parts humorous, relatable, and surprisingly sincere.

The game's strongest quality is its commitment to its central idea. Activities such as shopping, speaking with strangers, applying for work, and making acquaintances are treated with the same importance that traditional RPGs reserve for heroic quests. Through Bryce's perspective, even stepping into a crowded area feels like entering dangerous territory. This approach gives Introvert Quest a unique identity, particularly for players who have dealt with social anxiety or simply prefer solitude. Rather than mocking its protagonist, the game presents his challenges with an affectionate sense of humor, making his gradual development feel rewarding as the story progresses.

Narrative choices play a major role throughout the experience. Conversations frequently branch into multiple outcomes, and decisions can alter relationships, unlock different scenes, and influence the direction of Bryce's journey. The citizens of Sky City are an eclectic collection of personalities ranging from supportive companions to troublesome individuals, ensuring that exploration is consistently met with something unexpected. The writing embraces absurdity on occasion, but it never loses sight of its themes of self-improvement and personal growth. By the end of the adventure, players are encouraged to reflect on how much Bryce has changed from the anxious individual they first encountered.

Although storytelling remains the primary focus, Introvert Quest does not ignore its RPG roots. Turn-based battles appear throughout the game, adding variety to the dialogue-heavy pacing. Combat is straightforward and accessible, functioning more as a supplement to the narrative than a complex system requiring extensive strategy. Additional activities, including the Digital Duels mini-game, provide extra distractions and contribute to the sense that Sky City is a living place with its own culture and hobbies. The inclusion of a New Game+ mode further enhances replayability, offering new content and alternate perspectives that make a second playthrough worthwhile.

From a presentation standpoint, the title embraces its indie origins. Built with a visual style reminiscent of classic RPG Maker projects, it features simple environments and expressive character artwork that suit its contemporary setting. The soundtrack complements the mood effectively, shifting between lighthearted moments and more introspective scenes. While players expecting high production values may find the visuals modest, the game's charm comes from its personality rather than technical achievements. Every aspect of its design serves the narrative, reinforcing the feeling that this is a deeply personal project created with a clear vision in mind.

That said, Introvert Quest is not without shortcomings. Its pacing can occasionally slow during extended dialogue sequences, and some jokes land more effectively than others. Certain mechanics lack depth compared to larger role-playing games, and the limited budget is evident in parts of the presentation. However, these issues rarely overshadow the experience as a whole. The game's willingness to tackle an unconventional subject matter gives it a memorable quality that many independent RPGs struggle to achieve.

Ultimately, Introvert Quest succeeds because it understands that not every adventure needs to involve saving the world. Sometimes, the greatest challenge is finding the confidence to step outside, introduce yourself to someone new, and discover your place within society. Amaterasu Software delivers an experience that is quirky, heartfelt, and refreshingly different from genre conventions. It may not appeal to everyone, but players seeking a story-driven RPG with meaningful choices and an uncommon perspective will likely find plenty to appreciate in Bryce Han's journey.

Rating: 7/10
